boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Spanish Fort record (March 27-April 8, 1865) in the Mobile Campaign [March-April 1865]. Steele's march from Pensacola, the investment of Blakely (AL006), the reduction of Batteries Huger and Tracy and the occupation of Mobile are context or separate records. Campaign-wide marches, returns, prisoner totals and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads XVI and XIII Corps and Spanish Fort Garrison; the live field reads zero. Canby gives the army assembled at Mobile Point and Dauphin Island in mid-March as 13,200 of the Thirteenth Corps, 16,000 of the Sixteenth and 3,000 engineers, artillery and cavalry, 32,200 in all, and names the brigade and three divisions engaged in the final operations. Gibson gives his garrison as Thomas's Alabama Reserves of about 950 muskets, Patton's artillery of 360 and his own brigade of 500 rifles, later relieved and reinforced, and his force as less than 2,000 men against two corps and a fleet with over seventy-five guns on land. His own estimate of the Union muskets is illegible in OCR.
claims.rationale: A mid-March assembly figure for most of the army, a list of units in the final operations and a defender's garrison figures; no matched return. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. Canby says the works were taken by midnight with more than 600 prisoners while most of the garrison escaped by the treadway; Gibson says the garrison was withdrawn in good order, some skirmishers being left behind. NPS says most of the garrison escaped to Mobile.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 1,401 (US 657; CS 744); the live field reads 1,398 (US 657; CS 741). Canby reports more than 600 prisoners; the Spanish Fort block of his comparative statement is garbled in OCR and ends with the figures 52, 575 and 30, whose columns are not verified. Gibson gives 73 killed, 350 wounded and about half a dozen missing before the evacuation and estimates about 20 killed (read 2U), 45 wounded and 250 captured that night; he estimates the Union loss at 2,500. Canby says partial captured records give 73 killed and 120 wounded for Blakely and Spanish Fort together.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap.

open_questions: Gibson's subordinate reports, Holtzclaw's and Thomas's reports, and the Spanish Fort garrison returns remain deferred; C. C. Andrews's History of the Campaign of Mobile covers Spanish Fort but was not inspected for this record (three-family ceiling).

The organization and casualty returns (Nos. 2-3), the revised casualty statement on p.115, McAlester's engineer report, Granger's, A. J. Smith's, Steele's and the division and brigade reports, Maury's reports and the naval reports remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family (the NPS battle page plus the frozen Arnold rows). Canby's June 7, 1865 report and the comparative casualty statement printed with it (Official Records Series I, Volume XLIX, Part 1, No. 1) are one family of interested Union accounts. The Official Records volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge. Gibson's April 16, 1865 report from Meridian (No. 97) is one family of interested Confederate accounts; its OCR is badly garbled.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
